samples.title: Debit the asset, credit the capital - because
samples.subject: Accounting
samples.script: The owner deposits one hundred thousand rand as capital. Watch the double entry. Debit bank - an asset increases. Credit capital - the owner interest increases. Say the because aloud: every debit has its credit, and the accounting equation stays in balance. Assets equal owner equity plus liabilities: one hundred thousand equals one hundred thousand plus zero. Draw the skeleton first, post in the marked order, balance visibly. The numbers never lie - every figure you write must be traceable to this logic.
